# **Comprehensive Patent Intelligence and Structural Architecture Landscape for Modular Autonomous Mobile Robots (SIH26112)**

Modern intralogistics demands that autonomous mobile robots (AMRs) evolve from single-purpose transport platforms into flexible multi-mission bases capable of dynamically swapping functional superstructures, such as motorized conveyors, pallet scissor lifts, mobile manipulation arms, and vertical cart-towing interfaces1. However, the physical and electromechanical interface between the universal mobile base and interchangeable mission modules represents a severe structural bottleneck5. Commercial robotic platforms predominantly specify payload capacity as a lumped scalar mass, neglecting the coupled six-degree-of-freedom (6-DOF) dynamic wrench envelopes (![][image1]) induced by emergency deceleration, high-speed cornering, elevated centers of gravity (CG), dynamic manipulator reactions, and pallet transfer impulses5.  
Simultaneously, conventional topology optimization algorithms yield organic load-bearing geometries that encroach upon internal maintenance envelopes, obstructing rapid lateral battery extraction, wheel-motor replacement, and internal harness routing7. Furthermore, directly utilizing additively manufactured metals or polymers as primary structural contact interfaces introduces severe operational degradation, including fretting fatigue, bore ovalization, localized contact brinelling, bolt preload relaxation, and progressive datum loss9.  
Addressing these challenges requires a structural architecture that decouples kinematic registration from mechanical retention, isolates safety-critical sensor datums from chassis torsional strain, enforces serviceability keep-outs as formal negative obstacle bodies within generative synthesis, and incorporates field-replaceable hardened steel wear inserts within additive spaceframe nodes7.

## **Master Patent Landscape**

The global patent landscape surrounding modular AMR interfaces spans autonomous robotics, automated guided vehicles, robotic tool changers, machine-tool zero-point fixturing, aerospace payload adapters, and hybrid additive manufacturing7. The master landscape below compiles 32 foundational and contemporary patent families directly informing the structural, kinematic, and manufacturing boundaries of Smart India Hackathon 2026 Problem Statement SIH26112.

## **Patent Claim Decomposition of Key Prior Art**

Understanding the structural and legal boundaries of established technologies requires rigorous element-by-element deconstruction of the independent claims found in the fifteen most relevant patents.

### **1\. US 12,344,514 B2 — Mobile Industrial Robots A/S**

Deconstruction of Independent Claim 1:

> * Element A: An autonomous mobile robot system comprising an autonomous mobile robot base with a drive system12;  
> * Element B: A kit of parts comprising a plurality of functionally different top modules configured for mounting on the mobile robot base12;  
> * Element C: A mechanical receiving interface disposed on the upper side of the mobile robot base comprising standardized mounting apertures;  
> * Element D: An electrical interface providing electrical power and operational control communication between the base and the mounted top module;  
> * Element E: A control system configured to identify the mounted top module from the plurality of functionally different top modules and alter operational parameters based thereon12.

Analysis indicates that Elements A, B, C, and D represent mandatory physical limitations, while Element E serves as the functional limitation defining the inventive step12. The core novelty resides in tying standardized mechanical mounting holes to automatic software reconfiguration of vehicle kinematics12. This teaches the principle of eliminating manual technician commissioning when interchanging physical payloads. A candidate mobile robot base can design around this combination by abandoning centralized database lookups, instead embedding autonomous edge controllers within each attachment that communicate peer-to-peer over an EtherCAT bus, while substituting planar bolt holes with 6-DOF kinematic zero-point pull studs.

### **2\. US 12,263,888 B2 — Mobile Industrial Robots A/S**

Deconstruction of Independent Claim 1:

> * Element A: A chassis for an autonomous mobile robot comprising a monolithic moulded frame7;  
> * Element B: The frame having a top payload support surface providing rigidity to support payloads loaded thereon7;  
> * Element C: Rigid supporting elements integrally formed with or attached to the moulded frame to maintain sensor positions7;  
> * Element D: A plurality of separated compartments for electrical, electronic, and electromechanical (EEE) components7;  
> * Element E: The EEE compartments being accessible from the sides and ends of the mobile robot via detachable cover parts7;  
> * Element F: A central inside compartment and lateral outside compartments enclosed by a removable top cover7.

Elements A, D, and E are mandatory claim limitations7. The core novelty is the integration of rigid optical sensor datums directly into a single cast or moulded chassis monocoque that features compartmentalized, lateral maintenance service bays7. The patent demonstrates how structural mass can be configured to stabilize LiDAR coordinates relative to the driving surface7. A differentiated platform can achieve superior performance by avoiding a monolithic cast body altogether, utilizing instead a hybrid generative spaceframe composed of additively manufactured corner nodes joined by carbon-fiber composite tubes, while isolating optical sensor mounts on a kinematically decoupled carbon truss bridge7.

### **3\. US 8,005,570 B2 — ATI Industrial Automation, Inc.**

Deconstruction of Independent Claim 1:

> * Element A: A robotic tool changer comprising a master unit and a tool unit9;  
> * Element B: A coupling mechanism comprising a plurality of rolling members disposed circumferentially in the master unit9;  
> * Element C: A pneumatically driven piston movable along a first axis, the piston having a multi-tapered cam surface9;  
> * Element D: Wherein the multi-tapered cam surface comprises a first taper that forces the rolling members radially outward to contact a bearing race of the tool unit9;  
> * Element E: A second taper on the piston cam surface that forces the rolling members further outward into a locked position under high clamping force9;  
> * Element F: A fail-safe reverse taper surface interposed on the cam that prevents the rolling members from moving radially inward upon accidental loss of pneumatic locking pressure9.

Elements B, C, D, E, and F are all mandatory limitations, with the reverse fail-safe taper angle forming the essential core of novelty9. The engineering principle taught is mechanical amplification via compound angles combined with geometric trapping to prevent uncoupling upon fluid supply failure9. An alternative architecture circumvents this claim by eliminating ball bearings and pneumatic cylinders entirely, utilizing an electromechanically driven over-center toggle mechanism that drives flat-faced sliding wedges into retaining notches, relying on planar dead-center geometry rather than a reverse cam taper9.

### **4\. US 8,132,816 B2 — ATI Industrial Automation, Inc.**

Deconstruction of Independent Claim 1:

> * Element A: A robotic tool changer comprising a first unit and a second unit selectively couplable along a first axis11;  
> * Element B: A coupling mechanism at least partially protruding from the first unit to engage a recess in the second unit11;  
> * Element C: An electric motor operative to drive the coupling mechanism between coupled and decoupled positions11;  
> * Element D: Wherein the electric motor is coupled to the coupling mechanism by a rotating shaft disposed along a second axis perpendicular to the first axis11.

Element D represents the decisive limiting restriction of the claim11. Novelty is achieved by packaging an electromechanical tool changer within an ultra-low vertical envelope by placing the motor transversely and transmitting power via a perpendicular worm drive11. This teaches the principle of orthogonal drive packaging for high-force clamping within compact profiles11. A differentiated system can arrange the electric actuator coaxially with the clamping axis using a planetary roller screw, or position the rotary actuators on the removable module side rather than within the base mobile platform.

### **5\. US 7,422,204 B2 — SCHUNK GmbH & Co. KG**

Deconstruction of Independent Claim 1:

> * Element A: A clamping device for receiving a clamping pin attached to a workpiece or tool;  
> * Element B: A housing defining a central receiving bore along a clamping axis;  
> * Element C: A plurality of clamping slides arranged radially movable within the housing relative to the central bore;  
> * Element D: A spring assembly arranged within the housing urging the clamping slides radially inward toward the clamping pin;  
> * Element E: Wherein the clamping slides engage an annular locking groove of the clamping pin with tapered locking faces;  
> * Element F: A pressure chamber operable by fluid pressure to urge the clamping slides radially outward against the spring assembly to release the pin.

Elements C, D, and F represent mandatory claim limitations. The novelty centers on normally-closed, spring-applied radial slides that mechanically lock a tapered pull stud, relying on fluid pressure strictly for unlocking. This establishes the safety standard for zero-point fixturing: stored mechanical energy must supply the clamping force. A mobile robot interface can design around this by eliminating pneumatic release chambers entirely, adopting an electromechanical bistable toggle linkage preloaded by disk springs that locks past dead-center.

### **6\. US 10,486,756 B2 — KUKA Deutschland GmbH**

Deconstruction of Independent Claim 1:

> * Element A: An automated mobile transport vehicle comprising a vehicle chassis and a payload-carrying interface;  
> * Element B: The payload-carrying interface having three locating elements spaced apart on the vehicle chassis;  
> * Element C: Each locating element comprising a spherical engagement body;  
> * Element D: A detachable payload carrier having three matching receiving elements on its underside;  
> * Element E: Each receiving element comprising a V-shaped groove oriented radially toward a common center point;  
> * Element F: Wherein engagement of the spherical bodies within the V-grooves provides deterministic, overconstraint-free six-degree-of-freedom positioning.

The presence of three spherical bodies and three matching radial V-grooves (a classical Maxwell kinematic coupling) is mandatory. The core novelty is the direct implementation of Maxwell exact-constraint geometry on an automated guided transport vehicle. The physical principle demonstrates that exact constraint prevents internal stress accumulation from manufacturing variations or thermal expansion. However, spherical point contacts generate destructive Hertzian stresses under dynamic AMR shock loads. A superior alternative utilizes a quasi-kinematic coupling with line-contact cylindrical pins, or four-point planar zero-point tapers that distribute bearing stresses broadly across ground steel datums.

### **7\. US 11,285,622 B2 — BMW AG**

Deconstruction of Independent Claim 1:

Elements D and E are mandatory limitations that define the inventive step. Novelty rests on printing internal fluid ducts directly within a structural node to facilitate uniform adhesive distribution during chassis assembly. This teaches the utilization of additive geometric freedom to embed functional manufacturing aids within structural joints. A non-infringing mobile robot spaceframe avoids adhesive bonding entirely by utilizing split-collar clamp nodes that tighten mechanically around structural extrusions via external high-strength cross-bolts and reamed dowels, allowing rapid non-destructive field replacement.

Elements C and E are mandatory limitations. Novelty resides in printing internal centering ribs within multi-directional tubular sockets to mechanically control adhesive bond-line thickness. The physical principle establishes that structural adhesive performance depends heavily on maintaining an optimal, uniform shear gap. An alternative architecture avoids adhesive joints completely, using mechanical interference fits, split-clamp collars, or external taper sleeves that clamp onto structural chassis members.

Deconstruction of Independent Claim 1:

This validates the concept of embedding maintainability constraints into generative structural synthesis. A differentiated mobile robot design avoids routing corridors through internal node cavities, configuring the generative nodes as external corner brackets that cradle open, C-shaped structural extrusions defining an unobstructed, external transverse battery slide tunnel.

Elements C and D are mandatory limitations. This teaches the necessity of isolating sheet-metal covers from dynamic overturning moments. An alternative design eliminates intermediate adapter plates entirely by generatively synthesizing the AMR spaceframe such that the four corner zero-point docking receivers integrate continuous diagonal generative load paths that converge directly into the drive-axle and caster-bearing mounts.

Deconstruction of Independent Claim 1:

Elements D and E are mandatory limitations. The core novelty lies in using elastomeric decoupling elements to isolate an auxiliary sensor subframe from payload-induced chassis bending. This confirms that heavy payloads induce chassis deflections that tilt safety scanners into the floor, causing false emergency stops. A superior engineering alternative circumvents elastomeric damping (which suffers from long-term viscoelastic drift and high-frequency flutter) by mounting the optical sensors to a three-point kinematically mounted carbon-fiber datum bridge that anchors directly to non-deflecting wheel uprights via spherical flexures.

A differentiated implementation avoids motorized hooks by using a normally-closed mechanical over-center drawbar linkage, verifying physical metallic contact at the precision datums via dual-channel inductive safety sensors wired directly into the vehicle's Safe Torque Off (STO) circuit.

A differentiated platform focuses strictly on heavy industrial handling attachments (e.g., motorized roller conveyors, pallet lifters, and robotic manipulators) rather than tote-picking shelves, utilizing an active 6-DOF zero-point clamping interface rather than a passive tote-rack drop-in coupling23.

This teaches that tapered geometries eliminate mechanical clearance under clamping preload. An alternative mobile robot interface designs around horizontal tapered horns by utilizing a four-point vertical zero-point grid, where short-taper female locating cups embedded flush in the top deck receive vertical pull studs clamped via electromechanical cam slides.

## **Design-Pattern Extraction and Structural Principles**

Synthesizing global patent disclosures across robotics, machine tools, and aerospace reveals fundamental physical engineering principles that govern high-performance structural interfaces.  
The principle of deterministic decoupling of locating and clamping functions, demonstrated across US 7,422,204 B2, US 6,561,503 B2, and US 8,005,570 B2, resolves the mechanical conflict inherent in attempting to use a single element for both alignment and clamping9. High clamping forces induce asymmetric elastic deflection in alignment dowels, ruining datum repeatability, while clearance dowels permit micro-slip under dynamic shear. Separating functions allows precision short tapers to establish the six spatial datums (![][image32]) with zero clearance under light engagement force, while an independent mechanical drawbar or wedge applies heavy axial preloads normal to ground datum pads without exerting parasitic lateral forces. Broadly established in machine tools, this principle informs mobile robot design through four perimeter zero-point receivers where conical taper cups locate the module, while an internal spring-actuated sliding cam draws down a pull stud directly onto flat, hardened carbide datums.  
Direct load-path routing to suspension hard points, evidenced in US 10,870,205 B2, US 12,275,473 B2, and US 11,358,655 B2, addresses the structural compliance of intermediate chassis panels that amplifies dynamic moments15. When payload forces (![][image33]) are transferred into a horizontal top deck, the deck acts as a flexible diaphragm, transferring high bending moments into vertical side walls and causing chassis lozenging. Routing load paths along direct triangular generative struts connecting the module docking receivers directly to wheel suspension pivots and caster bearings resolves dynamic loads purely as tension-compression axial forces, maximizing system natural frequency. Within Autodesk Fusion Generative Design, this is implemented by designating preserve regions at the top module docking cups and wheel suspension mounts, generating structural trusses that bypass internal electronics envelopes entirely8.  
Normally-locked, fail-safe mechanical preload, seen in US 8,005,570 B2, US 9,566,688 B2, and US 7,422,204 B2, addresses the severe industrial hazard of systems requiring continuous fluid pressure or electrical current to maintain clamping9. A complete power interruption (such as an emergency stop or battery depletion) causes instantaneous decoupling under high-G braking. Utilizing stored mechanical energy (Belleville spring packs) or self-locking over-center geometry (![][image34]) guarantees retention under zero system power, requiring active energy strictly to release the clamp. This principle is realized via an electromechanical bistable over-center linkage preloaded by disc springs; when driven past center, the linkage locks against a physical stop, maintaining clamping force indefinitely without electrical draw.  
Wear cartridge decoupling for additive structures, informed by US 10,131,389 B2, US 11,285,622 B2, and US 11,760,250 B2, overcomes the material limitations of additively manufactured alloys. Laser powder bed fusion metals (such as AlSi10Mg) exhibit modest surface hardness (100–120 HV) compared to hardened tool steel (60 HRC / \~700 HV) and contain micro-porosity. Repeated high-cycle docking and dynamic cyclic fretting wear under warehouse vibrations cause rapid bore ovalization, thread stripping, and datum loss. Embedding field-replaceable, precision-machined tool-steel cartridge inserts into printed nodes transfers Hertzian contact stresses to superior alloys while preserving the lightweight organic geometry of the parent node. Precision-machined pockets in the generative nodes receive bolt-in hardened steel datum cups that can be replaced during scheduled maintenance without scrapping the primary printed chassis nodes.  
Kinematic isolation of metrology and sensor datums, revealed in US 11,498,630 B2 and US 12,263,888 B2, mitigates the effect of payload-induced chassis bending on safety sensors7. When an AMR carries an asymmetrical maximum payload (![][image35]), chassis flexure introduces angular pitch (![][image36]) and roll (![][image37]). An angular deflection as small as ![][image38] over a 10-meter scan radius projects the safety LiDAR field into the floor, triggering false emergency stops, or tilts it upward, creating a safety blind spot. Decoupling the sensor frame structurally from the payload spaceframe eliminates load-induced angular distortion. Mounting safety LiDARs on an internal carbon-fiber triangulated truss bridge anchored to non-deflecting wheel hub uprights via a three-point kinematic leaf-spring flexure isolates the sensor plane from top-deck load paths.

## **Expired, Abandoned, and Public-Domain Prior Art Opportunities**

Identifying expired, abandoned, and foundational public-domain patents establishes a solid technical baseline that can be freely implemented without licensing, provided active downstream improvements are avoided.  
US 7,422,204 B2, assigned to SCHUNK GmbH & Co. KG with a priority date of September 8, 2003, reached the end of its statutory 20-year patent term in September 2023\. The foundational concept of a zero-point clamping module featuring radial clamping slides urged inward by mechanical spring packs to clamp an annularly grooved pull stud, released by fluid pressure, has entered the public domain. The combination of a short-taper centering sleeve with a flat, ground axial datum face can be freely utilized. However, downstream active patents covering dual-piston turbo boosts, hermetic sealing slides, and integrated electronic inductive position sensors remain legally enforceable and must not be copied.  
US 8,005,570 B2, assigned to ATI Industrial Automation, Inc., with a priority date of January 14, 2005, expired in January 20259. The core mechanical disclosure—locking a master plate to a tool plate via ball bearings driven radially outward by an axial piston cam into an angled bearing race—is now public-domain mechanical art9. While the broad concept of a ball-lock changer is accessible9, ATI maintains active patents on diagnostic communication blocks (US 8,616,560 B2) and motorized worm-drive actuators (US 8,132,816 B2) that must be respected11.  
US 6,561,503 B2, assigned to AMF Andreas Maier GmbH & Co. KG, expired in July 2020\. This patent discloses spring-actuated ball-lock mechanisms for fixture plates where internal compression springs drive balls into an annular groove of a pull stud to achieve normally-closed clamping. The disclosed mechanics, spring calculations, and taper angles provide an open reference for fail-safe clamping without continuous power.  
US 5,915,678 A, assigned to System 3R International AB, expired in July 2017\. It discloses elastic-averaging pallet clamping chucks where resiliently deformable centering elements engage reference grooves on a pallet to achieve repeatable sub-micron positioning. The underlying mathematics of elastic averaging and ground datum pads remain completely open for engineering adoption.  
AU 2020216167 A1, filed by Locus Robotics Corp. with a priority date of January 30, 2020, was abandoned during prosecution23. The application disclosed specific tote-coupling geometries and drop-in shelf bracket arrangements for order-picking robots23. While the specific geometries disclosed in this abandoned application entered the public domain in Australia23, caution is required because Locus maintains active continuation families in the United States and Europe (such as US 11,724,395 B2 and EP 3,984,852 B1)21.  
US 4,576,481 A, granted to Alexander Slocum in 1986, is the foundational academic and industrial patent for three-groove Maxwell kinematic couplings. All statutory protection has long expired, placing the classical equations of kinematic constraint, contact stress calculation, and ![][image4] radial V-groove layouts into the permanent public technical knowledge base.

## **Indian Jurisdiction Patent Landscape and Freedom-to-Operate Considerations**

Conducting patent landscape research for a competition in India requires evaluating both global prior art standards and domestic territorial enforceability under the Indian Patents Act, 1970\.  
Under Section 2(1)(j) and Section 13 of the Indian Patents Act, an invention must possess absolute global novelty to be patentable. Any mechanical arrangement disclosed in a published patent document worldwide (such as a US, European, Japanese, or Chinese patent) serves as novelty-destroying prior art against an Indian patent application. Consequently, engineering concepts disclosed in foreign patents cannot be claimed as novel inventions by hackathon participants.  
Conversely, under Section 48 of the Act, patent rights are strictly territorial. A foreign patent granted in the United States or Europe grants no exclusive monopoly within India unless a corresponding application was filed with the Indian Patent Office (IPO) through the Patent Cooperation Treaty (PCT) National Phase within 31 months of the priority date. If a foreign patentee failed to file or let their application lapse in India, manufacturing, assembling, and operating that mechanism within Indian territory does not constitute patent infringement under Indian law.  
GreyOrange Pte Ltd maintains the most significant intralogistics robotics patent portfolio in India35, originating from its engineering and manufacturing operations in Gurugram35. Key granted and pending Indian patents include IN 352194 (corresponding to US 10,216,193 B2), which claims an automated guided vehicle comprising a drive chassis and an elevating platform driven by a central motor and transverse horizontal screws for lifting warehouse storage racks34; IN 378412 (corresponding to US 10,481,612 B2), which covers independent swing-arm drive-wheel suspensions that maintain traction under payload shifts34; and IN 201747012345 (corresponding to US 10,501,263 B2), which claims high-friction rotatable turntable engagement plates for mobile robots35. To maintain freedom to operate, the mobile base must avoid low-profile internal scissor lifts and central rotating turntables36.  
Addverb Technologies Limited, based in Noida, holds a growing portfolio of Indian filings (including IN 202111048912 A) focused on warehouse sortation shuttles, multi-directional carton shuttles, and fleet distribution algorithms37. Their filings emphasize track-switching wheels and AS/RS interfaces, leaving open space around modular 6-axis kinematic top-module docking interfaces for unit-load AMRs.  
Other domestic players, such as Ati Motors, ANSCER Robotics, and Hi-Tech Robotic Systemz, concentrate on autonomous outdoor tuggers, vision-based SLAM algorithms, and basic towing hitches35. Mechanical modularity in their portfolios is restricted to simple bolt-on deck configurations. Patent filings from Indian academic institutions (including IIT Madras, IIT Delhi, and IISc Bangalore) in robotics classification B25J 5/00 concentrate on multi-terrain crawling robots, pipe-inspection mechanisms, and reconfigurable serial linkages28, showing minimal coverage of high-load, repeatable quick-change structural interfaces for warehouse automation.  
Multinational corporations show varied filing strategies in India. KUKA Deutschland GmbH maintains active Indian patents on industrial 6-axis manipulator wrists, but did not pursue Indian national phase entry for its AGV kinematic coupling patent (US 10,486,756 B2). Dematic and the KION Group maintain Indian grants covering high-density automated racking and automated forklift masts28. Mobile Industrial Robots A/S (Teradyne) has not pursued Indian patent coverage for its core structural chassis patents (US 12,263,888 B2 and US 12,275,473 B2)7, creating an open manufacturing space within India for those structural concepts, even though global novelty standards prevent claiming them as new inventions7.

## **Strategic "Do Not Claim" Prior Art Boundary**

To ensure the SIH26112 project maintains high technical integrity and avoids presenting established prior art as novel during evaluations, the engineering team must treat the following twenty-two features as known art.  
The broad concept of a modular autonomous mobile robot base that accepts interchangeable functional attachments is extensively disclosed in US 12,344,514 B2 and commercial catalog platforms4. Generic topology optimization or generative design lightweighting applied to a mobile robot chassis frame is widely documented in automotive and robotics literature5. Fastening modular superstructures using standard quick-release over-center toggle clamps or quarter-turn quarter-twist studs is established tooling practice. Fabricating a mobile robot chassis as a monolithic moulded or cast body with lateral electronics compartments and rigid sensor bridges is directly claimed in US 12,263,888 B27.  
Robotic tool changers utilizing pneumatically driven ball-lock mechanisms with multi-taper cams and reverse fail-safe surfaces are covered in US 8,005,570 B29. Zero-point clamping modules utilizing spring-applied radial clamping slides with fluid-pressure release are claimed in US 7,422,204 B2. Implementing a classical three-groove Maxwell kinematic coupling using three spherical pins and three radial V-grooves on an AGV top deck is claimed in US 10,486,756 B2. Dynamically calculating and altering LiDAR protective safety fields in software based on vehicle speed and turning yaw rate is claimed in US 2024/0094737 A114.  
Pivoted bogie arm suspensions carrying modular traction ballast weights to adjust drive wheel friction are claimed in US 12,275,473 B215. Scissor-jack lift mechanisms driven by central motors and transverse horizontal lead screws nested inside an AMR chassis are claimed in US 10,216,193 B234. Vehicle spaceframe joints comprising additively manufactured metal nodes with integrally printed internal adhesive injection channels are claimed in US 11,285,622 B2. 3D-printed tubular chassis nodes featuring internal sockets with integrated centering ribs for bond-line control are claimed in US 10,286,960 B2.  
Generative chassis nodes featuring internal pass-through corridors for utility routing or tool access are claimed in US 11,167,804 B2. Motorized rotating hook latches equipped with position sensors that interlock with robot drive controls are claimed in US 11,858,573 B2. An autonomous mobile base featuring an upper deck coupling that receives an interchangeable tote-holder superstructure and tablet display mast is claimed in US 9,758,305 B2 and EP 3,984,852 B123. Intermediate structural adapter plates designed to route dynamic overturning moments from a robot arm directly to AMR suspension mounts are claimed in US 10,870,205 B2.  
Structurally decoupled sensor carrier frames isolated from payload-induced chassis bending moments via elastomeric damping elements are claimed in US 11,498,630 B2. Multi-axis compliant spring-loaded floating brackets for blind-mate electrical connectors are claimed in US 9,827,678 B239. Automatic module recognition using coded resistor dividers, RFID tags, or 1-Wire EEPROM chips is standard industrial electronics practice. Generating design geometry by defining preserve regions, obstacle bodies, and target loads is claimed as a software method in US 10,740,494 B28. Dual tapered engagement horns locked via transverse sliding wedges are claimed in US 11,760,250 B2. Finally, mounting a motorized roller conveyor directly to an AMR payload deck is standard commercial art3.

## **Defensible Engineering Innovation Zones for SIH26112**

Filtering out saturated prior art reveals six primary engineering opportunities where the SIH26112 platform can establish a genuine, defensible technical contribution.

### **Zone 1: Common Interface Engineered and Validated Against a 6-Axis Dynamic Wrench Envelope**

Rather than specifying payload capacity purely as a lumped mass (![][image52]), the interface is engineered around a mathematically bounded six-axis dynamic wrench boundary envelope ![][image53] that simultaneously bounds forces and moments:  
![][image54]  
The closest prior art, such as NASA’s US 11,989,009 B2 and ABB’s US 10,870,205 B2, handles multi-axis forces via active parallel Stewart platforms or custom intermediate adapter plates30. The proposed innovation decomposes dynamic moments (![][image5]) across four perimeter-mounted zero-point receiving modules spaced at ![][image55] and ![][image56]. This layout resolves overturning moments purely into push-pull vertical forces (![][image57]), ensuring that contact stresses remain strictly compressive across precision ground datum pads. The technical merit is validated within Autodesk Fusion Simulation by analyzing twelve distinct multi-axis dynamic load combinations, demonstrating positive joint separation margins under combined ![][image58] braking and ![][image59] turning.

### **Zone 2: Maintainability-Constrained Generative Chassis Architecture**

Addressing the tendency of generative optimization to produce organic structures that block internal component servicing, the proposed architecture models maintenance extraction envelopes as inviolable negative obstacle keep-outs7. While Divergent’s US 11,167,804 B2 claims internal wiring pass-through tunnels and Autodesk’s US 2023/0324882 A1 covers software-level obstacle generation8, the physical innovation here is an open spaceframe synthesized around three primary maintenance envelopes: a continuous transverse rectangular tunnel (![][image60]) for lateral battery extraction7, two vertical drop-down corridors for wheel-motor servicing7, and continuous tool-clearance conical obstacles projecting from all fastener locations8. The resulting generative spaceframe forms a skeletal arch truss that routes payload wrenches around the battery tunnel directly into suspension hard points, demonstrating high industrial serviceability8.

### **Zone 3: Hybrid Generative Nodes with Replaceable Precision Hardened Wear Cartridges**

Lightweight additively manufactured alloys (such as LPBF AlSi10Mg) suffer from fretting fatigue, surface galling, and bore ovalization when subjected to high-cycle industrial docking. Divergent’s US 10,131,389 B2 claims sacrificial crush inserts within printed nodes for vehicle crash energy absorption. The proposed engineering contribution implements a structural corner node that integrates split-clamp collars for structural carbon/aluminum extrusions, while isolating all kinematic locating and clamping contact into a bolt-in, CNC-machined A2 tool-steel cartridge (hardened to 60 HRC). The steel cartridge incorporates a female short-taper locating cup (achieving ![][image61] repeatability), a flat ground datum shoulder, and a transverse locking wedge channel. This confines the additive aluminum node to broad-area compressive bearing stresses (![][image62]), shielding the low-hardness printed metal from dynamic contact wear.

### **Zone 4: Sensor-Datum-Preserving Chassis Truss (Flexure-Decoupled Metrology Bridge)**

Heavy asymmetrical payloads induce chassis torsional twist, which tilts optical safety scanners (LiDAR) and leads to false emergency stops or dangerous blind spots7. Jungheinrich’s US 11,498,630 B2 isolates a sensor carrier frame using elastomeric damping elements, which introduce viscoelastic creep and high-frequency vibrational flutter. The proposed solution mounts the front and rear LiDAR sensors to a rigid carbon-fiber triangulated metrology bridge that connects to the primary chassis via a three-point kinematic leaf-spring flexure mount. Even when maximum asymmetrical payloads deflect the primary chassis by up to ![][image63] (inducing ![][image64] of frame twist), the kinematic flexures absorb the structural strain, maintaining LiDAR angular pitch within ![][image65] relative to the wheel contact datums.

### **Zone 5: Complete Physical Subsystem Separation within the Module Interface**

Prior-art interfaces, such as ATI’s tool changers (US 8,005,570 B2) and SCHUNK’s zero-point chucks (US 7,422,204 B2), integrate locating, clamping, and shear transfer into shared contact surfaces9. The proposed interface physically separates the five core interface functions into discrete, independently serviceable subsystems:

> * Locating is handled by four precision short-taper pins engaging hardened cups;  
> * Preload clamping is applied by four spring-actuated transverse sliding cams driven by an over-center linkage;  
> * Dynamic shear transfer is sustained by broad-area ground steel face collars engaging matching receiver shoulders;  
> * Electrical utility connection is isolated to a central multi-axis floating blind-mate docking block with gold-plated pogo pins;  
> * Wear mitigation is managed by field-replaceable hardened steel cartridge liners lining all contact zones.  
>   This eliminates cross-functional failure modes, such as alignment pins bending under dynamic shear or electrical connectors fatiguing due to deck deflection.

### **Zone 6: Electromechanical Dynamic Hardware Auto-Derating**

While MiR’s US 12,344,514 B2 identifies top modules via software and Clearpath’s US 2024/0094737 A1 modulates LiDAR fields in real time12, the proposed interface incorporates hardware-level cryptographic identification (via a 1-Wire EEPROM or resistor divider network inside the utility block) that directly constrains the low-level motion controller's maximum allowable linear acceleration (![][image66]), cornering yaw rate (![][image67]), and jerk (![][image68]) based on the attachment's specific physical 6-axis load envelope ![][image69]:  
![][image70]  
This links structural mechanics directly to vehicle motion planning, guaranteeing that the AMR cannot execute a trajectory that exceeds the physical wrench capacity of the mounted superstructure.

## **Closest-Prior-Art Risk Ranking and Differentiation Analysis**

The ten prior-art patents representing the most significant overlap risk to the proposed SIH26112 architecture are ranked below from highest to lowest severity, accompanied by detailed technical differentiation strategies.

### **1\. US 12,263,888 B2 — Mobile Industrial Robots A/S**

7  
This patent provides an AMR chassis that maintains rigid sensor alignment while organizing internal electronics into accessible side compartments7. The independent claim covers a monolithic moulded chassis frame with lateral and end access compartments, a removable top cover, and rigid integral sensor mounting structures7. The overlap risk is high if the mobile base is designed as a single monolithic cast or printed tub with side doors and direct sensor mounts7. However, it fails to cover hybrid spaceframes built from additive nodes and composite tubes, pass-through transverse battery slide tunnels, or kinematically decoupled sensor bridges. Differentiation is achieved by utilizing an open spaceframe with printed AlSi10Mg nodes and structural carbon-fiber tubes, while isolating the sensor frame on a three-point kinematic flexure mount7.

### **2\. US 12,344,514 B2 — Mobile Industrial Robots A/S**

12  
This patent enables a mobile base to receive different functional top attachments and alter its software parameters based on attachment identity12. The claimed scope covers an AMR system comprising a mobile base, a kit of interchangeable top modules, a mechanical interface, power/data connections, and automated module identification12. The overlap risk is high if the design claims the broad concept of an AMR platform with interchangeable modules and auto-identification12. However, it does not cover bounded 6-axis dynamic wrench interfaces, positive zero-point pull-stud clamping, DfAM hybrid nodes, or maintainability-constrained frames. Differentiation is achieved by focusing all claims on the specific kinematics of the four-point zero-point interface, the bounded 6-axis load envelope, and the maintainability-constrained generative nodes, treating software identification as background art12.

### **3\. US 8,005,570 B2 — ATI Industrial Automation, Inc.**

9  
This patent provides high-strength, zero-backlash, fail-safe locking for robotic tool changers9. The claimed scope covers master and tool plates locked via ball bearings driven outward into an angled race by an axial piston cam with a reverse fail-safe taper9. The overlap risk is extreme if pneumatic or motorized ball-locking mechanisms with multi-taper cams are used9. It fails to cover planar zero-point wedge cassettes, four-corner distributed chassis couplings, manual over-center toggle drawbars, or additive node integration. Differentiation is achieved by completely avoiding ball bearings and reverse-taper piston cams, implementing instead an electromechanical over-center toggle mechanism driving sliding wedge bars into pull-stud notches9.

### **4\. US 7,422,204 B2 — SCHUNK GmbH & Co. KG**

This patent provides zero-point clamping of workpiece pallets to machine-tool tables. The claimed scope covers a clamping module housing radially movable clamping slides urged inward by springs to lock a pull stud, with fluid pressure applied to open the slides. The overlap risk is high if miniaturized spring-clamped, pneumatic-released zero-point chucks with radial slides are used. It fails to cover electromechanical actuation, DfAM chassis node integration, mobile robotic payload decks, or 6-axis dynamic wrench monitoring. Differentiation is achieved by replacing fluid-released radial slides with a transverse eccentric cam or an over-center toggle linkage driven by a low-power stepper lead screw.

### **5\. US 11,498,630 B2 — Jungheinrich AG**

This patent prevents chassis bending moments from misaligning navigation and safety LiDARs. The claimed scope covers an automated transport vehicle with a payload frame and an auxiliary sensor carrier frame decoupled from the payload frame via elastomeric dampening elements. The overlap risk is moderate to high if an isolated sensor bracket is used to maintain LiDAR horizontal alignment. It fails to cover rigid kinematic leaf-spring flexures, carbon-fiber metrology bridges tied directly to wheel hub datums, or generative chassis integration. Differentiation is achieved by avoiding elastomeric bushings and implementing an exact-constraint kinematic flexure mount using three titanium leaf springs that insulate the sensor bridge from chassis strains while maintaining rigid rotational calibration.

### **6\. US 11,285,622 B2 — BMW AG**

This patent provides strong structural joints between additively manufactured metal nodes and standard spaceframe tubes. The claimed scope covers an additively manufactured vehicle node featuring profile sockets and integrally printed internal adhesive injection ducts. The overlap risk is moderate if chassis nodes are printed that join to tubes using internal glue channels. It fails to cover non-bonded mechanical split-clamp nodes, field-replaceable wear cartridges, or maintenance corridor obstacle geometries. Differentiation is achieved by eliminating adhesive bonding entirely, designing generative nodes with external split-clamp geometry secured via cross-bolts and reamed dowels for non-destructive field serviceability.

### **7\. US 10,216,193 B2 — GreyOrange Pte Ltd**

34  
This patent provides vertical lifting of storage racks within an ultra-compact AMR chassis envelope34. The claimed scope covers a mobile robot chassis enclosing a scissor-jack lift mechanism driven by a central motor and transverse horizontal screws34. The overlap risk is moderate if the Part-B functional attachment is an integrated chassis-embedded pallet scissor lift36. It fails to cover detachable modular top lifter attachments that mount externally to standardized zero-point chassis datums. Differentiation is achieved by ensuring the AMR base chassis contains no integrated lifting scissor links, packaging the Part-B pallet lifter as a self-contained, externally mounted modular attachment that clamps to the universal base interface and powers its own linear actuators via the blind-mate electrical bus36.

### **8\. US 11,858,573 B2 — Omron Corporation**

This patent provides automated electromechanical latching and safety interlock verification for mobile robot top modules. The claimed scope covers a mobile robot top surface with motorized hook latches and an interlock position sensor that inhibits base motion if unlatched. The overlap risk is moderate if motorized rotating latch hooks with limit switches are used. It fails to cover direct mechanical over-center toggle clamps, multi-axis pull studs, or zero-backlash short-taper registration. Differentiation is achieved by utilizing preloaded vertical pull studs engaged by transverse cam slides rather than rotating hooks, implementing dual-channel inductive proximity sensors monitoring physical metal flushness at the datum face, wired directly to Safe Torque Off (STO).

### **9\. US 10,286,960 B2 — Divergent Technologies, Inc.**

This patent provides lightweight vehicle chassis construction using generative 3D-printed nodes and connecting tubes. The claimed scope covers a vehicle spaceframe with printed nodes having multi-directional sockets with internal centering ribs for adhesive bonding. The overlap risk is moderate if a tubular spaceframe joined by 3D-printed metal corner nodes is claimed broadly. It fails to cover mobile robot maintainability keep-outs, battery slide-out tunnels, zero-point docking integration, or sensor datum isolation7. Differentiation is achieved by narrowing all generative chassis claims to the interaction between the generative load truss, the negative battery maintenance corridor, and the four-corner zero-point docking receivers8.

### **10\. US 2024/0094737 A1 — Clearpath Robotics Inc. / Rockwell Automation**

14  
This patent covers dynamic modulation of mobile robot safety fields during trajectory execution based on velocity and turning rate14. The claimed scope covers methods monitoring angular and linear velocity to dynamically recalculate and adjust LiDAR critical sensor regions14. The overlap risk is low to moderate if the AMR dynamically switches safety zones. It fails to cover physical mechanical chassis structures, kinematic decoupling, or zero-point clamping hardware. Differentiation is achieved by focusing the engineering contribution entirely on physical hardware and structural dynamics, leaving safety zone switching to standard COTS safety scanner firmware without claiming safety-field algorithms14.

## **Recommended Mechanical Architectures for SIH26112**

Based on the complete patent intelligence landscape, three distinct mechanical candidate architectures are synthesized. Each architecture resolves Gaps A, B, and C while circumventing active prior-art claims and maintaining full compatibility with Autodesk Fusion workflows39.

### **Candidate 1: Hybrid Generative Spaceframe with Integrated 4-Point Zero-Point Deck (Primary Recommendation)**

> * Base Chassis Concept: A lightweight, high-rigidity hybrid spaceframe comprising four corner nodes additively manufactured in AlSi10Mg via LPBF, joined longitudinally and transversely by high-modulus pultruded carbon-fiber tubes (![][image71] wall). The frame surrounds a central transverse battery extraction tunnel.  
> * Additive-Manufactured Components: Four corner generative load nodes that consolidate suspension pivot mounts, drive-motor anchor flanges, structural tube split-collars, and the female zero-point receiver cavity into a single lightweight topology; two central swing-arm bogie pivots transferring normal ground forces15.  
> * Conventional Components: High-modulus pultruded carbon-fiber tubes for chassis sills, 4140 pre-hardened steel cross-bolts for split-clamp node retention, and COTS industrial differential drive units with dual caster wheels7.  
> * Module Interface: Four-point symmetrical rectangular perimeter pattern (![][image72]).  
> * Locating Mechanism: Each corner node incorporates a precision short-taper female locating cup (![][image73] included angle) engaging a matching male tapered shoulder on the top module's pull studs.  
> * Locking Mechanism: Dual-shaft electromechanical eccentric over-center cam slide. A low-profile 24V DC planetary gearmotor drives two transverse shafts that displace hardened steel sliding wedges into annular locking grooves on the module pull studs, locking past dead-center with mechanical spring detents.  
> * Load-Transfer Mechanism: Vertical forces (![][image74]) and dynamic overturning moments (![][image5]) transfer through broad ground annular carbide datum pads surrounding each short taper. Lateral shear forces (![][image75]) and yaw moments (![][image76]) transfer through the short-taper contact interfaces.  
> * Replaceable Wear Elements: The female short-taper cups and flat datum pads are packaged as bolt-in A2 tool-steel cartridges (hardened to 60 HRC), secured into precision-machined counterbores within the additive aluminum corner nodes via four M5 flat-head screws.  
> * Electrical/Data Interface: Central blind-mate docking block featuring four high-current floating contacts (48V DC, 40A continuous bus) and a 16-pin gold-plated pogo-pin array for EtherCAT, STO dual safety loops, and 1-Wire EEPROM module ID, sealed to IP65 via a silicone bellows face gasket.  
> * Maintainability Strategy: The central chassis bay forms an uninterrupted transverse rectangular tunnel (![][image77]). The 48V 30Ah lithium battery pack unlocks via a single flush handle and slides laterally out of the chassis on nylon guide rails in ![][image78] without disturbing the top module7. Drive-motor wheel pods unbolt vertically downward as modular drop-out cassettes7.  
> * Part-B Functional Attachment: Powered bi-directional motorized roller conveyor deck designed for automated bin/tote transfer at conveyor transfer stations, featuring an internal 24V motorized drive roller (MDR), vulcanized polyurethane drive belts, and optical retro-reflective tote sensors.  
> * Autodesk Fusion Generative-Design Workflow: Preserve bodies are defined at four top zero-point receiver pockets, four suspension pivot brackets, two drive-wheel axle blocks, and four carbon-tube clamping collars8. Obstacle bodies represent the transverse battery tunnel volume (![][image79]), drop-out drive-wheel servicing envelopes, ground clearance boundary, and assembly bolt tool-access corridors8. Manufacturing constraints specify additive manufacturing with vertical build orientation (Z-up), maximum overhang angle ![][image80], and minimum wall thickness ![][image81]39.  
> * Required FEA Load Cases (Fusion Simulation): Emergency braking dynamic load (![][image58] deceleration with maximum ![][image82] payload at ![][image83] CG height: ![][image84]); high-speed cornering centrifugal torsion (![][image59] lateral acceleration: ![][image85]); conveyor cargo transfer shock (![][image86] vertical step-load on outer conveyor rail); and three-wheel ditch crossing chassis lozenging (![][image87] torsional twist across diagonal wheel pivots).  
> * Physical Prototype Approach: Additive corner nodes 3D printed via industrial FDM in carbon-fiber reinforced nylon (PA-CF12) with continuous strand reinforcement (or DMLS AlSi10Mg if metal printing sponsorship permits). Chassis rails fabricated from roll-wrapped carbon-fiber tubes. Wear cartridges machined from 4140 pre-hardened steel on a 3-axis CNC mill.  
> * Patent-Overlap Concerns: Avoids MiR US 12,263,888 B2 by using an open tubular spaceframe rather than a monolithic cast frame7. Avoids ATI US 8,005,570 B2 by using sliding cam wedges instead of ball-lock piston cams9.  
> * Genuine Engineering Contribution: Demonstrates that maintainability extraction corridors can be explicitly modeled as generative obstacle bodies to create a high-stiffness, field-serviceable mobile robot chassis with a bounded 6-axis dynamic zero-point interface8.

### **Candidate 2: Kinematically Decoupled Datum Base with Quasi-Kinematic Coupling**

> * Base Chassis Concept: A low-profile CNC-machined 7075-T6 aluminum bottom plate carrying drive units, overlaid by a perimeter structural spaceframe of 4040 heavy aluminum extrusions.  
> * Additive-Manufactured Components: Three additive titanium (Ti-6Al-4V) quasi-kinematic V-seat brackets mounted at ![][image4] on the top deck; four generative motor-mount uprights with integrated suspension dampers.  
> * Conventional Components: Precision ground 7075-T6 aluminum base plate (![][image88] thick), 4040 aluminum structural extrusions with drop-in T-nuts, and ground hardened 52100 chrome-steel dowel pins (![][image89]).  
> * Module Interface: Three-point quasi-kinematic layout.  
> * Locating Mechanism: Three hardened cylindrical steel pins on the module base seat into three precision V-shaped groove blocks oriented at ![][image4] toward the center, providing deterministic 6-DOF location with line-contact stress distribution.  
> * Locking Mechanism: Central high-load electromechanical drawbar. A central brushless motor drives a planetary roller screw, pulling a central ISO-standard retention knob on the attachment downward with ![][image90] of axial clamp force, seating the three quasi-kinematic pins into their V-grooves.  
> * Load-Transfer Mechanism: Quasi-kinematic line contacts carry combined shear (![][image75]) and vertical reaction loads (![][image74]), while the high central preload ensures zero pin lift-off under maximum overturning moments (![][image5]).  
> * Replaceable Wear Elements: The V-groove inserts are wire-EDM machined from D2 tool steel (62 HRC) and fastened into the additive titanium seats with countersunk screws.  
> * Electrical/Data Interface: Symmetrically placed dual pogo-pin docking arrays positioned on either side of the central drawbar, featuring floating compliance mounts (![][image91]) to prevent pin side-loading during clamping.  
> * Maintainability Strategy: The upper extrusion deck pivots open on heavy-duty rear hinges, supported by gas struts, revealing the entire interior electronics and battery bay for bench-top-level maintenance access in ![][image92].  
> * Part-B Functional Attachment: Compact high-payload scissor pallet lift capable of lifting standard warehouse euro-pallets (![][image93]) by ![][image94] for autonomous pallet transport, powered by self-contained dual electric ball-screw actuators driven from the AMR 48V power bus.  
> * Autodesk Fusion Generative-Design Workflow: Generative optimization of the scissor-lift lifting arms and base pivot brackets using 2.5-axis and 3-axis CNC milling constraints; topology optimization of the three titanium quasi-kinematic V-seat brackets under combined ![][image95] clamping and shear loads.  
> * Required FEA Load Cases (Fusion Simulation): Maximum pallet lift static vertical proof test (![][image96] downward); off-center pallet loading (![][image97] applied at extreme corner of lift platform: ![][image98] overturning moment); and quasi-kinematic line contact stress analysis verifying ![][image99] across V-groove surfaces.  
> * Physical Prototype Approach: Waterjet-cut aluminum 6061-T6 plate base, COTS aluminum extrusions, 3D-printed DMLS titanium or CNC-machined steel V-groove blocks, and an off-the-shelf electric scissor actuator.  
> * Patent-Overlap Concerns: Differentiates from KUKA US 10,486,756 B2 by using cylindrical line-contact quasi-kinematic pins rather than spherical point-contact balls. Avoids GreyOrange US 10,216,193 B2 by packaging the scissor lift entirely inside the detachable attachment rather than the base chassis34.  
> * Genuine Engineering Contribution: Demonstrates that quasi-kinematic line-contact mechanics can deliver sub\-![][image100] datum repeatability on heavy warehouse AMRs without experiencing the destructive Hertzian point-contact failure modes of classical Maxwell couplings.

### **Candidate 3: Full Monocoque Skeleton with Decoupled Sensor Truss**

> * Base Chassis Concept: A full monocoque skeleton frame wherein the entire structural perimeter and load paths are printed as four modular generative AlSi10Mg quarters, bolted together along longitudinal and transverse centerlines.  
> * Additive-Manufactured Components: Four modular generative chassis quarters bolted along neutral axes; one triangulated carbon-fiber/additive titanium sensor truss bridge.  
> * Conventional Components: Stainless steel linear guide rails and sealed ball bearing slides for the battery drawer, and COTS industrial brushless hub motors with integrated cycloidal drives.  
> * Module Interface: Standardized four-corner ISO twist-lock pattern.  
> * Locating Mechanism: Four corner-mounted diamond-and-round locating pins engaging precision bronze-bushed holes on the module base.  
> * Locking Mechanism: Manual single-throw over-center quadrant lever. A single flush-mounted side lever acts through a synchronized internal push-pull rod linkage to rotate four corner miniature 90-degree twist-lock heads simultaneously, snapping over-center with zero electrical power draw.  
> * Load-Transfer Mechanism: Vertical retention is carried by the 90-degree twist-lock flanges; horizontal shear (![][image75]) is transferred through the heavy cylindrical base collars surrounding each twist-lock stud.  
> * Replaceable Wear Elements: The twist-lock heads, shear collars, and locating pins are turned from 17-4 PH stainless steel, engaging replaceable Ampco 18 aluminum-bronze bushings press-fit into the generative chassis pockets.  
> * Electrical/Data Interface: Rear-mounted multi-pole blind-mate connector block with heavy silver-plated copper blade contacts for high-current power transfer and shielded twisted-pair contacts for fieldbus networks.  
> * Maintainability Strategy: The battery pack is mounted on a heavy-duty rear drawer mechanism with full-extension stainless steel slides; releasing an external latch allows the entire battery pack to roll smoothly out the rear of the robot for replacement in ![][image92].  
> * Part-B Functional Attachment: Collaborative 6-DOF robotic arm pedestal module mounting a Universal Robots UR10e or equivalent cobot arm, equipped with an integrated 24V vacuum pump end-effector and auxiliary battery pack for extended runtimes.  
> * Autodesk Fusion Generative-Design Workflow: Full chassis monocoque generative design utilizing additive manufacturing constraints with multiple load cases representing dynamic robot arm reactive moments (![][image101] dynamic); explicit optimization of the separate sensor truss bridge for maximum natural frequency (![][image102]) to eliminate vibrational resonance with the mobile drive base.  
> * Required FEA Load Cases (Fusion Simulation): Mobile manipulator emergency stop (articulated arm carrying ![][image103] payload at full extension of ![][image104] trips E-stop during ![][image105] velocity, producing a dynamic shock moment ![][image106]); sensor datum strain isolation (quantify angular deflection of LiDAR mounting surfaces under maximum chassis twist, verifying ![][image107]); and fatigue life evaluation under 2 million cycles of alternating dynamic torque.  
> * Physical Prototype Approach: Large-format FDM printing of chassis quarters using Carbon-PEEK or PAHT-CF15 filaments on an industrial high-temperature printer, assembled with grade 12.9 fasteners and CNC-turned stainless steel locking hardware.  
> * Patent-Overlap Concerns: Differentiates from Jungheinrich US 11,498,630 B2 by using a rigid kinematic three-point flexure mount for the sensor bridge rather than elastomeric damping elements. Avoids Omron US 11,858,573 B2 by using a purely manual over-center multi-stud linkage rather than motorized hook latches.  
> * Genuine Engineering Contribution: Quantifies and proves the structural decoupling of safety LiDAR coordinate datums from dynamic payload-induced chassis bending moments in modular AMRs, eliminating sensor misalignment trips under extreme dynamic moments.

## **Final Synthesis**

### **1\. What is already patented**

Global patent registers disclose that modular autonomous mobile robot platforms are heavily protected across several specific implementation methods7. These include standardized AMR top mounting decks that communicate electronically with functional top modules to alter software navigation parameters (MiR, US 12,344,514 B2)12; monolithic cast or moulded chassis bodies featuring integrated lateral maintenance bays and rigid optical sensor mounts (MiR, US 12,263,888 B2)7; pneumatically actuated ball-lock tool changers utilizing multi-taper cams and reverse-angle fail-safe mechanical locking surfaces (ATI, US 8,005,570 B2)9; zero-point fixture receivers utilizing spring-clamped radial wedge slides with fluid-pressure release (SCHUNK, US 7,422,204 B2); dynamic calculation and adjustment of 2D/3D LiDAR safety scanning fields based on monitored vehicle velocity and yaw rates (Clearpath/Rockwell, US 2024/0094737 A1)14; compact chassis-embedded scissor lifts driven by horizontal lead screws (GreyOrange, US 10,216,193 B2)34; additively manufactured spaceframe nodes containing integrally printed internal adhesive injection ducts (BMW, US 11,285,622 B2); printed vehicle spaceframe nodes featuring internal utility and tool-clearance pass-through corridors (Divergent, US 11,167,804 B2); elastically isolated auxiliary subframes carrying safety LiDARs on driverless transport vehicles (Jungheinrich, US 11,498,630 B2); and motorized latch hooks with limit-switch safety interlocks for mobile robot attachments (Omron, US 11,858,573 B2).

### **2\. What is already commercially solved**

The commercial intralogistics robotics market has fully commoditized several core modular features:

> * Swappable top superstructures—such as motorized roller conveyors, pallet lifters, shelf-tote racks, and cart towing hooks—are standard catalog offerings from OEMs including MiR, OTTO Motors, Omron, ROEQ, and Geek+2;  
> * Differential drive and omnidirectional drive-steer wheel assemblies with passive spring-damper suspension compliance5;  
> * Integrated planar LiDAR safety scanners with dynamic protective-field switching based on vehicle speed14;  
> * Automated cart towing via motorized locking pins or pintle hooks (such as the MiR Hook or Waypoint Kingpin)1;  
> * Automated goods-to-person shelf lifting via central electric ball screws (exemplified by the GreyOrange Butler and Geek+ P800)34;  
> * High-cycle blind-mate charging contact blocks utilizing copper-beryllium spring blades17.

### **3\. What is old technology but useful to us**

Foundational mechanical mechanisms whose patent terms have expired provide high-value, open-source building blocks for the SIH26112 platform:

> * Zero-Point Pull-Stud Workholding (AMF US 6,561,503 B2; SCHUNK US 7,422,204 B2): Spring-loaded mechanical clamping of tapered pull studs delivers zero backlash and high rigidity without requiring active hydraulic or pneumatic power during transport;  
> * Over-Center Toggle Linkages (Aviation Cargo US 5,487,629 A): Mechanical linkages driven past dead-center provide high mechanical advantage and fail-safe retention;  
> * Three-Point Quasi-Kinematic Couplings (Slocum US 4,576,481 A): Hardened cylindrical pins making line contact inside V-grooves provide deterministic registration while suppressing Hertzian point-contact stresses;  
> * Intermodal Twist-Locks (ISO 1161 / US 1,489,451 A): Rotating 90-degree lock heads separate axial tension from shear, carrying dynamic shear through broad cylindrical collars;  
> * Elastic Averaging Reference Strips (System 3R US 5,915,678 A): Resilient ground contact ribs absorb machining tolerances to achieve micron-level repeatability.

### **4\. What mechanisms appear safe only as inspiration**

Several patented mechanisms offer valuable engineering principles but cannot be copied directly due to active patent claims:

> * Multi-Taper Cam Ball-Locking (ATI US 8,005,570 B2): Inspires mechanical amplification and reverse-angle fail-safe trapping, but must be implemented via planar sliding wedges or eccentric cams rather than axial ball-locks9;  
> * Fluid-Released Radial Slide Clamping (SCHUNK US 7,422,204 B2): Inspires fail-safe spring preload, but fluid power must be replaced with electromechanical lead screws or manual over-center toggles;  
> * Dynamic Sensor Field Modulation (Clearpath US 2024/0094737 A1): Inspires accounting for payload inertia during stopping, but software field modulation should be avoided in favor of physical kinematic sensor-datum preservation14;  
> * Adhesive-Duct Additive Nodes (BMW US 11,285,622 B2): Inspires hybrid metal-node spaceframe construction, but adhesive bonding must be replaced with mechanical split-clamp collars;  
> * Elastomerically Decoupled Sensor Frames (Jungheinrich US 11,498,630 B2): Inspires isolating LiDAR datums from chassis bending, but elastomeric mounts must be replaced with rigid three-point kinematic leaf-spring flexures.

### **5\. What areas are patent-dense**

> * General modular AMR payload decks utilizing planar bolt patterns with standard CAN/EtherCAT pin connectors12;  
> * Chassis-embedded scissor-jack and screw-driven pallet lifting mechanisms34;  
> * Pneumatic and motorized robotic wrist tool changers9;  
> * Dynamic calculation of safety scanner protective zones based on vehicle kinematic parameters14;  
> * Automated cart towing hooks and hitch latches1.

### **6\. What areas remain underexplored**

> * Common AMR interfaces rated, bounded, and validated against a Six-Axis Dynamic Wrench Envelope (![][image1]) rather than scalar payload mass;  
> * Generative spaceframe chassis where internal maintenance extraction corridors (battery slide-out and drive-unit drop-down) are enforced as formal negative obstacle keep-outs7;  
> * Hybrid generative AlSi10Mg structural nodes incorporating field-replaceable, precision-machined, hardened tool-steel wear and datum cartridges;  
> * Decoupled kinematic sensor bridges that preserve LiDAR optical coordinate calibration under dynamic payload-induced chassis bending moments7;  
> * Physical subsystem separation where locating, preloading, dynamic shear transfer, utility pass-through, and wear mitigation operate as independently replaceable hardware modules;  
> * Hardware-level dynamic derating enforcing linear acceleration and cornering limits matched to the attachment’s specific 6-axis moment capacity.

### **7\. The 10 most useful patents for our engineering design**

> 1. US 7,422,204 B2 (SCHUNK): Teaches short-taper pull-stud mechanics and the complete separation of centering from clamping;  
> 2. US 8,005,570 B2 (ATI): Demonstrates mechanical fail-safe locking geometry and high mechanical advantage9;  
> 3. US 11,989,009 B2 (NASA): Provides the mathematical framework for 6-DOF dynamic load resolution across multi-point structural interfaces13;  
> 4. US 11,498,630 B2 (Jungheinrich): Highlights payload-induced chassis flexure as the root cause of safety LiDAR misalignment;  
> 5. US 10,740,494 B2 (Autodesk): Defines the mathematical implementation of preserve and obstacle bodies in generative structural synthesis8;  
> 6. US 10,131,389 B2 (Divergent): Teaches integrating replaceable inserts within additively manufactured vehicle nodes;  
> 7. US 11,760,250 B2 (Toyota): Illustrates short-taper horn geometry for high-load multi-axis shear transfer;  
> 8. US 5,487,629 A (Ancra): Details self-locking over-center mechanical toggle clamp geometry;  
> 9. US 4,576,481 A (Slocum / MIT): Details kinematic constraint equations and V-groove datum geometry;  
> 10. US 9,827,678 B2 (Stäubli): Details multi-axis compliant floating mounts for blind-mate electrical connectors39.

### **8\. The 10 patents we must study to avoid overlap**

> 1. US 12,263,888 B2 (MiR): Avoid monolithic moulded chassis tubs with integral side EEE compartments and sensor bridges7;  
> 2. US 12,344,514 B2 (MiR): Avoid broad claims covering an AMR base with interchangeable modules and auto-identification12;  
> 3. US 8,005,570 B2 (ATI): Avoid axial pneumatic piston cams driving balls outward into tool races with reverse fail-safe tapers9;  
> 4. US 8,132,816 B2 (ATI): Avoid electric motor-driven transverse worm shafts actuating tool changer ball-locks11;  
> 5. US 10,216,193 B2 (GreyOrange): Avoid compact scissor lifts driven by horizontal transverse lead screws inside the AMR chassis34;  
> 6. US 10,486,756 B2 (KUKA): Avoid classical three-groove Maxwell ball-and-groove kinematic couplings on AGV decks;  
> 7. US 11,285,622 B2 (BMW): Avoid additive spaceframe nodes with internal printed adhesive injection ducts;  
> 8. US 10,286,960 B2 (Divergent): Avoid printed tubular node sockets with internal adhesive stand-off ribs;  
> 9. US 11,858,573 B2 (Omron): Avoid motorized rotating latch hooks coupled to drive-inhibit safety limit switches;  
> 10. US 2024/0094737 A1 (Clearpath/Rockwell): Avoid claiming software algorithms that dynamically modulate safety zones based on turning yaw rate14.

### **9\. The 5 strongest cross-industry technologies to borrow principles from**

> 1. Machine-Tool Zero-Point Fixturing: Short-taper locating studs preloaded against flat ground datum pads to decouple alignment from clamping;  
> 2. Aerospace Kinematic Mounts: Three-point kinematic leaf-spring flexures to insulate precision optical sensor datums from primary structural frame deflections;  
> 3. Intermodal Freight Twist-Locks: Heavy base shear collars that carry 100% of horizontal dynamic shear loads, relieving the locking drawbar of bending stress;  
> 4. Aircraft Cargo Roller-Track Latches: Low-profile over-center toggle clamps that remain locked under zero electrical power;  
> 5. Precision Metrology Quasi-Kinematic Couplings: Replacing point contacts with cylindrical line contacts to reduce Hertzian contact stresses while maintaining high datum repeatability.

### **10\. Three recommended SIH26112 architectures**

> * Primary Architecture: Hybrid Generative Spaceframe with Integrated 4-Point Zero-Point Deck (Candidate 1). Additive AlSi10Mg corner nodes joined by carbon-fiber tubes, an internal negative obstacle battery tunnel, four corner zero-point receivers with replaceable A2 tool-steel wear cartridges, and a motorized roller conveyor attachment8.  
> * Secondary Architecture: Kinematically Decoupled Datum Base with Quasi-Kinematic Coupling (Candidate 2). CNC 7075 aluminum plate base with 4040 extrusions, 3-point cylindrical line-contact quasi-kinematic seats, central electromechanical drawbar, flip-up service deck, and a modular scissor pallet lift36.  
> * Tertiary Architecture: Full Monocoque Skeleton with Decoupled Sensor Truss (Candidate 3). Large-format printed AlSi10Mg monocoque quarters, four-corner manual over-center ISO twist-locks, rear slide-out battery drawer, 3-point kinematic flexure sensor bridge, and a collaborative 6-DOF robotic arm pedestal.

### **11\. What we should explicitly NOT claim as innovation**

> * The broad concept of a modular AMR or AGV accepting interchangeable top attachments4;  
> * Generic topology optimization or generative lightweighting of a mobile robot chassis5;  
> * Standard quick-release latches, over-center toggle clamps, or quarter-turn fasteners;  
> * Scissor-jack or screw-driven pallet lifting mechanisms within mobile robots34;  
> * Standard roller conveyor decks or passive drop-in tote carriers23;  
> * Standard pneumatic ball-lock tool changers9;  
> * Three-groove Maxwell ball-and-groove kinematic couplings;  
> * Automatic module recognition via RFID, coded resistors, or CAN node IDs;  
> * Velocity-dependent dynamic LiDAR safety field switching in software14;  
> * Preserve and obstacle bodies as a general CAD concept (patented by Autodesk)8.

### **12\. What we can plausibly claim as our engineering contribution**

> * A common modular AMR structural interface characterized, bounded, and validated against a six-axis dynamic force/moment envelope (![][image1]), transferring multi-axis dynamic loads through a four-point zero-point layout;  
> * A generative design optimization framework for AMR spaceframes where internal battery slide corridors and drive-unit drop-down envelopes are modeled as formal negative obstacle keep-outs7;  
> * A hybrid structural node architecture combining additive AlSi10Mg generative geometry with bolt-in, field-replaceable hardened tool-steel wear and datum cartridges;  
> * A modular interface that physically separates locating, preloading, dynamic shear transfer, electrical utility coupling, and wear management into discrete, independently serviceable subsystems;  
> * A structural chassis architecture wherein dynamic payload-induced torsional and bending deflections are kinematically decoupled from safety-critical optical sensor datums via a three-point flexure-mounted metrology bridge7.

### **13\. Patent questions that remain unresolved**

> * Territorial Status of Divergent Spaceframe Patents in India: Divergent Technologies filed multiple PCT applications covering 3D-printed nodes (such as US 10,286,960 B2). A complete prosecution status search in the Indian Patent Office (InPASS) is required to determine whether corresponding Indian National Phase filings were granted, abandoned, or are currently pending.  
> * Enforceability of Locus Robotics Tote-Interface Patents in Asia: Locus Robotics maintains active patents on picking AMR bases and tote couplings in the US (US 9,758,305 B2) and Europe (EP 3,984,852 B1)23. Their Indian filing status remains ambiguous across international registers, though foreign grants stand as global prior art that prevents patenting identical tote-holder drop-in features in India.  
> * Scope of GreyOrange Suspension Swing-Arm Claims: GreyOrange holds active Indian patents (IN 378412 / US 10,481,612 B2) on swing-arm suspension systems for warehouse robots34. The mechanical boundary between GreyOrange’s swing-arm linkages and standard industrial trailing-arm or bogie suspensions requires formal legal claim construction if custom suspension arms are fabricated15.

### **14\. Exact patent documents/figures our mechanical team should study before starting CAD**

> * US 12,263,888 B2 (MiR) — Figure 2 and Figure 6: Inspect to understand how commercial AMRs compartmentalize electronics bays and anchor LiDAR sensors, ensuring the generative spaceframe avoids duplicating their monolithic moulded layout7.  
> * US 8,005,570 B2 (ATI) — Figure 3A, Figure 3B, and Figure 5: Study the multi-taper cam, locking ball raceways, and reverse fail-safe surface to understand zero-backlash clamping mechanics, ensuring the cam-slide mechanism avoids their specific ball-lock claims9.  
> * US 7,422,204 B2 (SCHUNK) — Figure 1 and Figure 3: Analyze the cross-sectional interaction between the short-taper locating sleeve, the ground planar datum face, and the pull-stud annular groove to understand the physical decoupling of centering from clamping.  
> * US 11,498,630 B2 (Jungheinrich) — Figure 2 and Figure 4: Study the load-deflection diagrams illustrating how asymmetrical payload mass deforms the base chassis and tilts safety sensors, demonstrating the necessity of our decoupled sensor bridge.  
> * US 2023/0324882 A1 (Autodesk) — Figure 4 and Figure 11: Study the definition of tool-access keep-out cones and manufacturing accessibility obstacles within generative design setups8, directly informing how to configure the negative battery corridor obstacle body in Autodesk Fusion8.
